Responder's cuebid of the overcaller's suit: agreed 2026-11-04.

problems.explanation: Partner opened 1♥ and East overcalled 2♦. You have three hearts and 16 HCP: game values, maybe more. Cuebid the overcaller's suit: 3♦ shows support for partner's suit and a limit raise or better. Partner rebids 3♥ with a minimum, and you go on to game.

whyNot.2H: A simple raise shows about 6-10. You have 16.
whyNot.4H: A jump to game over an overcall is weak and distributional, to make it hard for the opponents. Partner would never look for slam with extras.
whyNot.X: A negative double shows four spades. You know you have a heart fit, so show it.

problems.explanation: Partner's 3♥ shows a minimum opening, with nothing extra to say. Your cuebid promised a limit raise or better, and with 16 HCP you have game opposite any opening: bid 4♥. With 12-14 opposite your 16, slam is out of reach.

whyNot.P: Your 3♦ showed a limit raise or better, and with 16 you have more than a limit raise. Game opposite any opening.
whyNot.4N: Partner has shown a minimum: 12-14 with your 16 isn't enough for slam.

reviewNotes: Hands and auction transcribed from the video's screenshots. Double dummy, NS take 11 tricks in spades and EW's 4♥ is one down.
Two cuebids: East's 2♠ (responder's, in the overcaller's suit, agreed 2026-11-04) and South's 3♥ (advancer's, in the opener's suit, agreed 2026-11-04).

problems.explanation: Partner opened 1♥ and North overcalled 1♠. You have three hearts and 10 HCP with a good six-card diamond suit: a limit raise in hearts. Cuebid the overcaller's suit: 2♠ shows heart support and a limit raise or better, so partner knows how strong the hand is when the bidding gets competitive.

whyNot.2H: A simple raise shows about 6-10 and a minimum hand. With 10 HCP and good diamonds, you're worth a limit raise.
whyNot.3H: A jump raise in competition is weak, a preempt. Cuebid to show a good raise.

problems.explanation: Partner overcalled 1♠ and the opponents have shown a heart fit. You have three spades, 10 HCP and a singleton diamond. Cuebid opener's suit: 3♥ shows support for partner's spades and a limit raise or better. Partner then knows the hand is ours and can judge whether to compete to 4♠.

whyNot.2N: Not with three spades: show the fit first.
whyNot.3S: A jump raise of an overcall is weak: four trumps and under 10 points. You have the values for a limit raise.
whyNot.4S: A direct jump to game is preemptive too. Cuebid first, so partner knows your strength.

deals.setAside: We know the Unusual 2NT but don't play it, and a defense to it is one convention more than we want for now (2026-11-05).
reviewNotes: Hands and auction transcribed from the video's screenshots. East played 5♣ and took five tricks: six down, +600 for North-South. Double dummy, 4♥ makes, and so does 5♦ for East–West.

problems.explanation: Partner opened 1♥ and East's 2NT shows both minors, at least five of each. You have four hearts, a singleton diamond and 10 HCP: a limit raise. Over the Unusual 2NT, cuebid the lower of their suits: 3♣ shows support for partner's suit and a limit raise or better, just as a cuebid does over an ordinary overcall.

whyNot.3H: A simple raise shows about 6-10 and a minimum hand. With four trumps and a singleton, you're worth a limit raise.
whyNot.4H: Jumping to game over their bid is weak and distributional, to shut them out. Partner would never know you have real values.
